QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_43

question.text: Which of the following about the 'Catch-up' clause in a Cat III fund is MOST ACCURATE?

answer.text: Catch-up is mandatory under SEBI (AIF) Regulations for all Cat III AIFs
Catch-up is rare in Cat III AIFs; when included, a 100% catch-up means the manager gets the entire residual above hurdle until the manager's pre-determined profit share is met
Catch-up applies only in open-ended Cat III AIFs
Catch-up is a regulatory risk metric similar to VaR

explanation.text: The Logic: Catch-up is contractually agreed, not mandatory, and is RARE in Cat III AIFs (common in Cat I/II PE). A 100% catch-up means residual profit after hurdle flows ENTIRELY to manager until their predetermined share is met; thereafter, residual split applies. The Trap: A overstates regulatory mandate. C/D are fabrications. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II) tests PE-style 100% catch-up as primary; XIX-E flags it as rare in Cat III.
